title: Verdant Harbor - control scout: SSO/KMS/RBAC audit

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-08-07 09:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jasmine (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Li (Redwood SE), Avery (Verdant Harbor Head of Platform), Samir (Security Architect), Rita (Compliance), Devin (DevOps)

[00:00] Jasmine: Hey everyone cc: thank you for joining, really appreciate you carving out time. Well do a quick intros then jump into security controls and your hosting preferences.
[00:18] Avery: Thanks, Jasmine. Short background — Verdant Harbor runs B2B SaaS for maritime logistics, lots of customer PII and regulatory needs in EU and US, so security and data residency are big.
[00:30] Samir: Right, were evaluating whether Redwood hosted will meet our compliance or if we need dedicated or private. Main gates are SOC2 evidence, SSO integration (SAML), RBAC, detailed audit logs, and KMS/BYOK.
[00:44] Marco: Great, thats exactly the checklist others have used. Quick outline from our side — Hosted (fastest), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools w/ tenant isolation), Private (VPC/on-prem for strict residency). There are tradeoffs around latency, cost, and control over keys.
[01:05] Rita: On SOC2, we need Type II plus the last six months of controls; also ISO27001 is in our roadmap — do you have either?
[01:14] Jasmine: We do SOC2 Type II and current ISO attestation is in process. Ill attach the SOC2 report after the call. Note: some vendor names in the report might be redacted.
[01:23] Samir: Fine, but well need the control mapping — mapping of Redwood controls to our control framework.
[01:30] Jasmine: Yes, we can provide a controls matrix.
[01:33] Devin: Quick Q on SSO — we use SAML 2.0 with Okta and SCIM for provisioning. How mature is your SAML/SCIM support?
[01:42] Li: We support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for provisioning. Theres a standard SAML metadata exchange, and SCIM v2 for provisioning groups/users. There are a couple of known quirks with some IdPs where nameID formats cause mismatches, but we have a checklist.
[01:58] Samir: Do you support enforced MFA at IdP, session timeouts, and session re-authn for admin operations?
[02:07] Marco: We delegate auth to your IdP for SSO sessions. Admin ops in Console are RBAC-protected; we surface session creation timestamps and session termination APIs. We support SAML attributes for group membership to map roles.
[02:22] Rita: For RBAC, we need role separation: platform-admin, infra-ops, compliance-viewer (read-only logs), and app-service accounts. Can your teams map fine-grain permissions to these roles?
[02:34] Li: Yes — our RBAC model supports resource-level permissions (model endpoints, deployments, audit logs) and we can add custom roles. Marco: Weve seen customers define about 8-12 roles to stay manageable.
[02:47] Samir: How about service accounts and key management? We want keys to be customer-managed (BYOK) with automatic rotation every 90 days and HSM-backed storage (FIPS 140-2).
[03:00] Marco: Dedicated and Private support BYOK. Hosted supports an envelope encryption pattern where your KMS (KMS in your cloud) can be used to wrap keys in some plans. For HSM/FIPS, dedicated/private can integrate with HSM-backed KMS or on-prem HSM appliances.
[03:18] Avery: So with hosted wed lose BYOK? Thats the tradeoff?
[03:21] Jasmine: Hosted has options — we have a hosted tier that allows customer-managed keys (theres some integration work), but the highest control (full HSM in customer's VPC) is only with Private.
[03:33] Devin: What about at-rest encryption for model artifacts and cache? And transit? Do you have TLS everywhere?
[03:38] Li: All traffic in transit is TLS 1.2+; at-rest encryption is AES-256. Model artifacts and KV cache are encrypted by default. If you opt for BYOK, keys are wrapped by your KMS.
[03:51] Rita: Audit logs — granularity and retention. We need immutable logs for admin auth changes, model deployments, inference requests for audit sampling. Retention policy target is 18 months for logs and 7 years for certain audit artifacts. Is that feasible?
[04:08] Marco: We can export audit logs to your storage (S3/GCS/Azure Blob) with a configurable retention. Our default retention in hosted is 90 days; dedicated can be extended, and private gives you full control. For 7-year archival, customers use exported buckets with lifecycle policies.
[04:24] Samir: How real-time is the log export? We need near real-time for alerting.
[04:29] Li: We push logs to a streaming endpoint — typical delivery within seconds to minutes. For near real-time alerting youd forward into your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog).
[04:38] Avery: Any information on tokenization and PII redaction before logs? Wed prefer PII not appear in logs.
[04:46] Marco: We redact certain prompt fields by default in hosting — but prompt-level auditing can be configured. If you need to avoid storing raw prompts, we can use prefix/KV caching strategies that avoid logging content, or redact at ingestion. We should map exactly which fields you consider PII.
[04:59] Samir: Data residency — some EU customers require EU-only processing. Can Redwood guarantee region pinning for hosted requests?
[05:07] Jasmine: Yes, region routing policies are supported. Hosted can pin to EU regions; Dedicated can be placed in specific regions; Private obviously runs in your VPC. We do cross-region fallbacks only if allowed by policy.
[05:21] Rita: Regarding SOC2 evidence — we will need to get the SOC2 report and also evidence of encryption controls, key rotation schedules, and incident response playbooks.
[05:32] Jasmine: We'll provide the SOC2 Type II and an overview of key management controls and playbooks. Some of the deeper artifacts require an NDA but we can share redacted extracts.
[05:42] Devin: Latency/tradeoffs — if we go dedicated to meet residency/BYOK and fine-grain logging, what's overrun on cost and latency compared to hosted?
[05:52] Marco: Dedicated is higher fixed cost but gives predictable throughput and locality. Latency is comparable to hosted in the same region; the biggest delta is cost model — dedicated has committed units. We can run a quick bench with your sample requests to show per-token latency and throughput.
[06:06] Avery: On the RBAC side, does Redwood support SCIM group sync so we can manage access via Okta groups?
[06:12] Li: Yes, SCIM group sync is supported. You can map SCIM groups to Redwood roles. Well share the SCIM schema and a short checklist for Okta.
[06:21] Samir: One subtlety — we want an immutable audit trail for any admin changes, with who changed what and before/after values for role grants. Does your audit do diffs?
[06:31] Marco: We record admin actions with metadata and old/new values for config-like changes. For some actions we include diffs; for others we include snapshots. We also persist the actors identity (SAML subject) when available.
[06:44] Rita: For compliance, we also need a record of subprocessor locations and a data processing addendum.
[06:50] Jasmine: We'll provide a subprocessor list and DPA template.
[06:54] Devin: Any known issues integrating with our custom key rotation policy? We do forced 90-day rotations and emergency key revocation.
[07:02] Marco: Emergency key revocation is supported on Dedicated/Private. Hosted supports revocation in our wrapped-key model but there are steps to rewrap and re-encrypt artifacts which wed coordinate with your team.
[07:14] Samir: For performance-sensitive endpoints well probably want dedicated pools; can we do a hybrid where critical workloads use Dedicated and lower-sensitivity use Hosted?
[07:23] Li: Absolutely — smart routing can route by policy (latency, cost, or sensitivity). You can set rules to send certain traffic to dedicated pools and fall back to hosted variants if capacity is low.
[07:35] Avery: Great. Quick question on data deletion: if a customer asks for data to be deleted, how quickly can you remove cached keys or prompt history?
[07:44] Marco: We support deletion APIs; cached KV/prefix caches can be purged. Retention windows apply to exported logs. For hosted, depending on SLA, deletion may take up to X hours to propagate; for Private you control retention fully. Well provide exact SLAs in the follow-up.
[08:00] Rita: Well need to validate the deletion flows as part of our PIA.
[08:05] Jasmine: Noted. Well include a deletion flow doc in the follow-up pack.
[08:12] Li: One operational note — when you bring BYOK, you own key rotation and Redwood needs a rewrap window to re-encrypt stored artifacts. We have a standard rewrap handshake to avoid downtime.
[08:26] Samir: Sounds good. Anything else on your side we should know?
[08:30] Jasmine: Two quick asks — 1) can you send a short list of the controls youre most concerned about (we heard RBAC, KMS, audit logs, SSO), and 2) confirm stakeholders for next call (security, platform, devops).
[08:42] Avery: I will send a two-page control priority doc. Also will invite our infra lead to the bench test.
[08:49] Jasmine: Great. To close, well circulate SOC2, KMS whitepaper, RBAC template, SAML/SCIM checklist, and draft connectivity tests.
[08:58] Rita: Thanks.
[09:00] Meeting end.
